The Federal Aviation Administration and the Department of Transportation marked the launch of a federal electric vertical takeoff and landing pilot program in Texas, a move intended to accelerate planning for air-taxi operations and shape future urban air mobility standards in the United States. Joby Aviation began demonstration flights under this effort, signaling a concrete step toward operationalizing advanced air mobility beyond the conceptual phase [FAA and Transportation Secretary Sean P. Duffy marked the launch](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMilwFBVV95cUxNQmxQcFBSX0VUcHlYb0M5RFQ4X2FfYW84djUyazFmb3dpWHdXV09lRXlZdmIxb1NpRVlLNlpJNnp1RW8zQVBydTllWUhaVnh6TnJEN3VlLTZBc2pleTRWUzlWdXp1bnNVTlBHTHhPRTFHUERvZWFLR1lXM0EwX21wbXA2RVBGVHdHWmJsOGR5ek1ZX3U5RmxB?oc=5). This initiative represents a significant federal commitment to integrating new aircraft types into the national airspace system, providing a regulatory pathway for commercial electric air mobility.

In the autonomous vehicle sector, Spain granted its first Level 4 autonomous-vehicle permit to a consortium including Uber, WeRide, and Avomo, clearing the way for robotaxi testing in Madrid [Spain granted its first Level 4 autonomous-vehicle permit](https://news.google.?oc=5). This international milestone highlights the growing global competition in high-level autonomy, as jurisdictions outside the United States begin to authorize fully driverless passenger services. The approval suggests that regulatory frameworks for Level 4 autonomy are maturing rapidly in key European markets, potentially influencing future U.S. policy discussions and industry expansion strategies.

Defense and counter-drone capabilities saw significant commercial activity, with AeroVironment announcing it received its first international order for the LOCUST directed-energy counter-drone system, a deal reported at more than $50 million [AeroVironment said it received its first international order](https://www.uasvision.com/2026/09/11/av-gets-first-international-order-for-locust-directed-energy-counter-drone-systems/). Simultaneously, Volatus Aerospace said it won a five-year contract to supply drones to the Canadian Army [Volatus Aerospace said it won a five-year contract](https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/articles/volatus-aerospace-awarded-five-contract-170217982.html). These transactions indicate a robust international demand for advanced unmanned systems and directed-energy technologies, reflecting a broader trend of allied nations investing in modernized air defense and unmanned aerial capabilities.

In rail infrastructure, the Federal Transit Administration delivered $233 million to modernize rail transit infrastructure [The FTA delivered $233 million](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiowFBVV95cUxOTHllUnMyTVQ3bm1tM1hfT21fdU9wclZJTlRrbFd4UE5wMFpuYVJxdmNyVzFtTkJBT0pWRlBxRUc5QVRoR1VMd0lJY2M5WVlGWlc5U1FPS1A5QVVEeG5hMElFX3VJOE01b0xhMkliQWthQUdJd1Jsd0QzS21Pd0xBam1YV1pEM0wycXByWUI0NGxHMjFUUVk3TkF4YTlWV0RxMVpz?oc=5). This funding supports the upgrade of existing transit systems, addressing critical maintenance and modernization needs in major U.S. cities. The allocation underscores the federal government’s continued focus on improving the reliability and capacity of public transportation networks as part of a broader advanced transportation strategy.
